title: Rework accessibility for skeleton loaders and loading states in dense tables
creator: Sophia Nguyen
description: Audit and remediate accessibility issues caused by skeleton placeholders and animated loading states in dense data tables and list widgets. Current problems reported from support and accessibility audits: screen readers either read empty table structures repeatedly or announce misleading content during initial render, keyboard focus can land on non-interactive skeleton cells, and shimmer animations fail contrast heuristics in high-contrast / dark themes. We need a consistent pattern and implementation guidance for skeletons, progressive-loading tables, and edge cases (row virtualization, server-side pagination, keyboard focus during streaming rows). Deliver a design spec, implementation checklist, automated tests, and VPAT evidence for these components.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec that defines ARIA roles/attributes for skeletons vs content (what to announce and what to hide)
Implementation pattern that uses aria-hidden, role=status or role=progressbar, and clearly documented live-region politeness settings
Keyboard navigation does not stop on skeleton elements; focusable controls only appear when actual content is interactive
Shimmer/animation contrast meets motion & contrast guidance and can be disabled by prefers-reduced-motion/settings
Unit / integration tests verifying screen reader announcements for: initial loading start, incremental row load, loading complete (NVDA/VoiceOver/TalkBack smoke checks)
VPAT evidence page updated with screenshots, test notes, and pass/fail rationale for sections related to tables and dynamic content
implementation_steps: Run an audit across the component library to list all table and list variants that use skeletons (virtualized tables, paginated lists, small/compact rows)
Create a design token mapping for placeholder colors in light/dark/high-contrast themes and ensure WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratio for non-text graphical indicators

Define ARIA rules: set skeletons to aria-hidden=true by default; for overall progress use a single container with role=status (polite) or role=progressbar when measurable; announce row counts only after content is available
Add a 'placeholder-state' CSS utility with reduced-motion and accessible fallback styles; document how to opt-out per customer preferences
Update keyboard-focus behavior: ensure tab order skips placeholder cells (tabindex=-1), and make sure focus is placed on a safe landing element when navigating into a partially-loaded table
Implement automated test scenarios in the component test harness (storybook/cypress): simulate slow network, stream rows, virtualized windowing, and validate aria attributes and announcements
Produce a VPAT annex with steps performed, test environment (OS, screen reader version), and links to test logs and visual evidence
Ship a small migration guide for apps that used to rely on empty cells to be focusable or to be read by screen readers
design_notes: Prefer a single role=status live region placed outside the table for polite incremental announcements (e.g., 'Loading 8 of 32 rows') to avoid repetitively announcing table structure
Avoid placing live regions on each skeleton cell; that produces excessive verbosity in screen readers
When table row count is known, show a progressbar with aria-valuenow/aria-valuemax while rows are streaming; use role=status for unknown totals
Make shimmer purely decorative (aria-hidden) and provide a non-animated high-contrast fallback that meets contrast requirements
For keyboard users, when keyboard focus would otherwise land in a skeleton cell, redirect focus to a visible control (e.g., 'Show row when available' placeholder button) or skip it entirely
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Some integrations rely on focusable empty cells for automation. Mitigation: provide a migration guide and a temporary opt-in legacy flag.
Risk: Announcements may be noisy if we mis-configure live regions. Mitigation: QA with NVDA/VoiceOver/TalkBack and add a QA checklist item for announcement frequency limits.
Risk: Visual regressions in compact table density. Mitigation: include visual regression snapshots for every theme and density combination.
Risk: Customers expecting row-count immediately. Mitigation: document behavior and provide a code pattern for pre-known-count progressbars.
testing_matrix: Mac + Safari + VoiceOver: initial load, incremental row load, focus traversal with keyboard
Windows + Chrome + NVDA: streaming rows, aria-hidden verification, progressbar semantics
Android + TalkBack: virtualized lists and focus behavior during scroll
High-contrast / inverted colors: verify placeholder visibility without violating contrast
Automated: cypress integration tests to assert aria attributes and storybook snapshots for reduced-motion setting
